articles.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
articles.description: The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image was the work of hundreds of scientists and captured the first direct view of a black hole's shadow—becoming one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. A team of four from CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, has developed a powerful new imaging technique that validated the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An independent technique has validated the landmark 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of M87*, confirming the first direct visual evidence of a black hole. This independent verification strengthens confidence in one of astronomy's greatest achievements.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA has announced an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028 with SpaceX and Blue Origin leading development efforts. This ambitious goal marks a thrilling new chapter in lunar exploration and human spaceflight.

articles.title: Voici comment la NASA compte coloniser la Lune dans six ans
articles.description: La NASA compte bien établir une base permanente sur la Lune. Elle a dévoilé son plan, point par point.
articles.summary: NASA has unveiled its comprehensive plan to establish a permanent lunar base within six years, marking a transformative milestone in human space exploration. This ambitious goal represents a major step toward sustained human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
articles.description: SpaceX could make history with the world's first full recovery of an orbital rocket and spacecraft on Starship Flight 15.
articles.summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 15, which could achieve the historic first full recovery of an orbital rocket and spacecraft through a synchronized double-landing maneuver. This breakthrough would revolutionize spaceflight economics and reusability.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's historic milestone of traveling one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after launch, inviting public participation in commemorative activities.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy.  […]
articles.summary: NASA scientists reveal how the upcoming LISA observatory will detect gravitational waves to discover new exoplanets and unlock mysteries of the universe.

articles.title: Planets Don't Just Disappear, But They Can Wobble Out of Sight if Their Neighbour is Close Enough
articles.description: TESS watched an exoplanet about 1,000 light years away as it repeatedly transited in front of its star for seven years. But astronomers were surprised to find that the hot Jupiter disappeared. Of course, planets don't just disappear. Something interrupted its transits from our point of view, and astronomers think they've figured out what happened. An unseen, nearby giant planet companion tugged on it until TESS couldn't see it anymore.
articles.summary: TESS observations reveal how gravitational interactions between exoplanets can cause orbital wobbles that create apparent disappearances in transit measurements.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: NOM4D demonstrates breakthrough capabilities in automated assembly of large structures in space, building on decades of ISS and space station construction experience.

articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of cosmic hydrogen clustering across large scales, revolutionizing methods for mapping the universe.

articles.title: Asteroid mining will crash the platinum market, but that's good news for Earth
articles.description: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. Humanity is slowly getting closer to that reality. But if you ask asteroid mining skeptics, they will usually ask one specific question—what happens to the prices of all those rare materials once someone actually brings them back? A pair of system dynamicists from MIT directly tackled that question with a new paper titled Will AstroForge Collapse the PGM Market?
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Asteroid mining technologies could harvest precious metals like platinum from space, revolutionizing resource availability on Earth. This advancement promises transformative benefits for humanity through sustainable access to rare materials.

articles.title: Centaurus A in the spotlight: Plasma simulations reproduce black hole jets' mysterious bright edges
articles.description: Around 12 million light-years away, the supermassive black hole of the galaxy Centaurus A is hurling two enormous plasma jets into space at nearly the speed of light. These so-called jets are brighter at their edges than at their center. The reason for this was previously unclear but has now been explained by a team from the Chair of Astronomy at the University of Würzburg. The research is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Plasma simulations have successfully reproduced the mysterious bright edges of black hole jets observed in Centaurus A, 12 million light-years away. This breakthrough enhances our understanding of how supermassive black holes channel enormous energy into space.

articles.title: Bennu asteroid analysis suggests unexpected origins for organics in space
articles.description: Samples from the Bennu asteroid, which is currently more than 200 million miles (322 million kilometers) from Earth, and the Murchison meteorite, which fell to Earth in 1969, both contain molecules that build proteins necessary for life. New research has found that the molecules may have formed through the same process but originated far from one another in the solar system.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu reveals unexpected origins for organic molecules in space, suggesting new pathways for the building blocks of life. This discovery expands our understanding of chemistry in the cosmos.

articles.title: Earliest known compact quasar pair poses a black hole growth puzzle
articles.description: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The earliest known compact quasar pair, observed only 900 million years after the Big Bang, presents new puzzles about rapid black hole growth in the early universe. This discovery challenges existing models of cosmic evolution.

articles.title: How ripples in space-time can reveal new exoplanets
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets—worlds beyond our solar system—throughout our galaxy.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The LISA observatory in development will detect gravitational waves to reveal new exoplanets, opening an entirely new detection method beyond traditional techniques. This revolutionary approach promises to uncover worlds previously invisible to astronomy.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
articles.description: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's CHAPEA crew has successfully completed over a year of simulated Martian life in isolation, providing invaluable data for human Mars exploration. This milestone represents crucial preparation for humanity's future on the Red Planet.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot has made history by autonomously constructing a structure in space, demonstrating revolutionary potential for future space construction projects. This breakthrough opens possibilities for robotic assembly of orbital infrastructure.

articles.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
articles.description: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.
articles.summary: Advanced James Webb imaging techniques have revealed hidden exoplanets previously invisible in telescope data, promising to uncover countless additional worlds. This breakthrough could dramatically expand the known catalog of alien planets.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Fresh volcanic activity detected on Mars suggests the planet may still have geothermal processes occurring beneath its surface. This discovery reveals Mars remains more geologically dynamic than previously thought.

articles.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
articles.description: NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for Mars Sample Return (MSR), called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture.
articles.summary: NASA launches an ambitious new Mars Sample Return initiative using the Perseverance rover to collect and bring Martian samples back to Earth. This groundbreaking mission will advance our understanding of Mars' geology and search for signs of ancient microbial life.

articles.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
articles.description: This dazzling collection of ancient stars could hold clues to the Milky Way's past.
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captures a stunning collection of ancient stars whose mysterious origins may unlock secrets of the Milky Way's formation and history. This breathtaking image reveals the cosmos' ancient beauty.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for astronauts to live and work on the Moon in an exciting new initiative. This historic opportunity marks humanity's next steps toward sustained lunar exploration and settlement.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, bringing us closer to understanding the exotic particles hidden in the zeptoverse. This breakthrough represents a major step forward in fundamental particle physics.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: New nanohertz gravitational-wave observations have provided constraints on supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn, offering insights into the early universe. This research combines cutting-edge gravitational wave detection with cosmological discovery.

articles.title: Tras un año de espera en el espacio la misión ESCAPADE de la NASA pone por fin rumbo a Marte usando la gravedad de la Tierra
articles.description: Tras casi un año justo en el espacio las dos sondas de la misión ESCAPADE de la NASA utilizaron estos días la gravedad de la Tierra para coger impulso hacia Marte, su destino definitivo. En concreto ESCAPADE Blue llevó a cabo su máxima aproximación el sábado …
articles.summary: After nearly a year in space, NASA's ESCAPADE mission has successfully used Earth's gravity to begin its journey toward Mars, demonstrating advanced orbital mechanics. This dual-spacecraft mission will unlock new discoveries about the Martian atmosphere.

articles.title: Les mystères de Mercure, ou comment la sonde BepiColombo va étudier la planète la plus proche du Soleil (sans tomber dedans)
articles.description: Après une mise en orbite d’une exquise complexité, la sonde européenne BepiColombo a un programme chargé. En effet, de nombreux mystères entourant la planète Mercure résistent toujours aux scientifiques.
articles.summary: The European BepiColombo spacecraft is undertaking an ambitious mission to study Mercury, navigating the extreme challenges of orbiting so close to the Sun. This mission will revolutionize our understanding of our solar system's innermost planet.

articles.summary: NGC 4449, a small but dynamically important galaxy, demonstrates how smaller galaxies can have outsized cosmic impact through gravitational interactions and star formation activity.

articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 10 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Saturn Behind the […]
articles.summary: A stunning celestial alignment captures Saturn positioned behind the Moon, offering a beautiful reminder of the dynamic geometry of our solar system.

articles.title: The Ice Giants' Magnetic Fields are Very Strange Compared to Earth's
articles.description: Uranus and Neptune, the Solar System's ice giants, have interiors unlike the other planets. As a result, they also have magnetic fields unlike the others. They're messy and tilted, and Voyager 2, the only spacecraft to even flyby them, showed us how messy they are. New research uses models to try to understand what's going on with the pair of planets and their weird fields, and found that it's likely they change on very short timescales. They could already be much different than when Voyager 2 visited in the late 1980s.
articles.summary: Scientists reveal the fascinating and unique magnetic field configurations of Uranus and Neptune, shaped by their unusual planetary interiors and exotic compositions.

articles.title: Asteroid Mining Will Crash the Platinum Market, But That’s Good News for Earth
articles.description: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. Humanity is slowly getting closer to that reality. But if you ask asteroid mining skeptics, they will usually ask one specific question - what happens to the prices of all those rare materials once someone actually brings them back? A pair of system dynamicists from MIT directly tackled that question with a new paper titled Will AstroForge Collapse the PGM Market?
articles.summary: Future asteroid mining ventures promise to revolutionize resource availability on Earth by harvesting platinum and other valuable materials from space.

articles.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
articles.description: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory distinguishes between Luminous Blue Variable stars and supernovae explosions, advancing our understanding of stellar phenomena.
